Google made Gemini 4 Argon generally available on October 13, 2026, but I could not open Google's own blog post. Everything below comes from third-party coverage that describes it, so check the official post before relying on specifics.

**What changed on October 13:** Google said on Oct. 13 that Gemini 4 Argon is now available to developers and enterprises through the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini platform. Access is also expanding to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity and to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

**Earlier access:** The company had first unveiled Argon to a limited group of cybersecurity partners on September 30, so the October update broadens availability rather than marking the model's first announcement.

**API identifier:** The changelog entry for 13 Oct 2026 says: "Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon) generally available (GA)." One source notes that for the model itself the documentation uses "now available" and "Stable." In practice the meaning is the same, since there is now a stable identifier without a preview suffix.

**Pricing:** The introductory API price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, 2026. After the offer expires, the announced rates are $4 for input and $20 for output per million tokens. Sources disagree on the exact switch date: one says from December 1 the price doubles to $4 and $20.

**Context window:** Argon has a unified 1,048,576-token budget shared by input, thinking and output. Default synchronous output is capped at 65,536 tokens.

**Caveat on performance claims:** One source notes that Google's benchmark and capability claims are vendor-reported and should be validated against a team's own workload.

Meta announced **Muse Spark Open** on October 15, 2026, and released its weights the same day. Sources describe it as Meta's most capable open-weight model so far.

- **Launch and claims:** Meta launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers. Alexandr Wang called it "the most capable US open-weight model to date".
- **Specs:** TechRepublic reports 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active parameters per token via a mixture-of-experts design, and a 1-million-token context window.
- **Focus:** Meta says the model is built for coding and agentic work. It is also "optimised" to run on Apple's advanced M5 Ultra chips. Meta engineered it with Apple's MLX framework so that two Mac Studio desktops equipped with M5 Ultra chips operate together over a unified memory pool.
- **Availability:** The release is available immediately as downloadable weights across Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, and Microsoft Foundry Models.
- **License:** The weights are not under a standard open-source license. Meta is using the "Muse Model License." Meta describes it as having "limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free."

Some of the search results conflict on the timeline. A Mugglehead article dated August 2026 describes Zuckerberg announcing plans to open-source its Muse Spark 1.2 model. Orcarouter says Meta announced on August 10 that it would open the weights of Muse Spark 1.2. The Register describes an earlier promise that Meta would release open weights for its flagship model "soon", alongside the Muse Spark 1.3 release. The results don't clearly establish whether the October Muse Spark Open release is the same model as the August-announced 1.2 weights, or a separate release. The October reports are the most direct coverage of the release itself, so I'd check Meta's own blog post to confirm the version name and timing.

DeepSeek released V4.1 Flash on September 10, 2026, according to most of the sources I found, though a few details differ between them.

**Release and availability**
- One source says the new model became available on September 10, 2026, under the API name deepseek-flash. Another says the lab announced it in a thread on X and published the weights on Hugging Face under the MIT licence.
- A Chinese-language report describes an earlier limited beta, starting September 8, under a temporary model name, with the test set to expire on September 10. The API name it gives differs from the one in the other sources, so that detail may be outdated.
- Older Flash model names will continue to work as aliases but now route requests to V4.1 Flash.

**Replacements and retirements**
- The release replaces its previous V4 Flash and V4 Flash Vision Experimental models.
- From 04:00 UTC on 14 September, DeepSeek will send every request made to V4-Pro, its top model, to V4.1-Flash instead. That routing runs until a V4.1-Pro arrives., and DeepSeek gave no date for it.

**Architecture and capabilities**
- The model has 552 billion parameters in total, and it activates 8 billion parameters per token when reading input and 16 billion when writing output.
- It handles up to 1 million tokens of context and understands images natively, according to its model card.
- Its maximum output is up to 384,000 completion tokens.
- Developers can adjust reasoning effort from 1 to 100, allowing them to balance cost and accuracy.

**Performance and pricing**
- DeepSeek says it beats its own flagship on coding and agent tasks, at a lower price. Independent verification is lacking: none are independently verified.
- Listed API prices differ by provider. OpenRouter lists $0.30/M input tokens and $1.20/M output tokens, with separate rates for Cache Read at $0.006/M tokens. LLM Gateway lists a starting price of $0.15/M input tokens and $0.60/M output tokens.

The sources I checked are secondary coverage plus DeepSeek's own announcements, and I did not open DeepSeek's official site directly. If you need exact pricing or API names, check DeepSeek's API documentation.

xAI released Grok Voice 3.0, a speech-to-speech model for its real-time voice agent API, on October 14, 2026. Here's what the search results say:

**Release and access**
- The model is available through xAI's Voice Agent API, and agents on the `grok-voice-latest` alias were moved to it automatically. One source says it replaced Grok Voice 2.0 behind the grok-voice-latest alias at the same price. The model ID is `grok-voice-3.0`.
- Pricing is $0.08 per minute, the same rate as Grok Voice 2.0. A separate $0.004 charge applies per text input.
- Based on the release notes that one article quotes, the API endpoints and session parameters are unchanged, so existing code shouldn't need edits. Sessions pinned to 2.0 will need to move to 3.0, since 2.0 is now deprecated.

**Performance claims**
- xAI says it ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Index at 86.9, with latency under one second. For comparison, Grok Voice 2 scored 81.3 on that index, per one report.
- Other figures cited from xAI include a task success rate of 94.8% and 98.5% on Big Bench Audio (speech reasoning).
- Latency is a tradeoff. One comparison table lists time to first audio at 0.81 seconds, up from 0.70 seconds for 2.0, so it starts speaking slightly later.

**Conflicting claims**
- xAI's API landing page calls it the "#1 Tau Voice Leaderboard," but one review says that Artificial Analysis's own τ-Voice run places Grok Voice 3.0 in 2nd place, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra). The reviewer suggests the two sides may be citing different leaderboards.

**Real-world use**
- xAI says the model powers voice in Tesla vehicles and the voice mode of Grok Bot, and handles Starlink support calls, with about 70% of 20,000 daily calls resolved without a human.

Most of these details come from secondary coverage and aggregator sites rather than xAI's own documentation, so check the official xAI docs before relying on the benchmark numbers or pricing.

content.text:
Estos son los tres lanzamientos más destacados entre el 11 y el 18 de octubre de 2026:

1. **Meta Muse Spark Open (15 oct.)**: Meta publicó los pesos de Muse Spark Open, un modelo MoE de 816.000 millones de parámetros (42.000 millones activos) con 1 millón de tokens de contexto, pensado para programación y agentes, que la empresa presenta como el modelo abierto estadounidense más capaz hasta ahora; se distribuye con una licencia propia, no de código abierto estándar. [TechRepublic](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-meta-muse-spark-open-apple-mac-studio/)

2. **Google Gemini 4 Argon, disponibilidad general (13 oct.)**: Google abrió su modelo de frontera Gemini 4 Argon a desarrolladores y empresas a través de Gemini API, AI Studio y Google Cloud, y también a los suscriptores de pago en la app de Gemini y en AI Mode, con un precio de lanzamiento de 2 $/10 $ por millón de tokens de entrada/salida. [Let's Data Science](https://letsdatascience.com/news/google-releases-gemini-4-argon-for-scientific-computing-644a49ff)

3. **xAI Grok Voice 3.0 (14 oct.)**: xAI lanzó su nuevo modelo de voz a voz en tiempo real para su Voice Agent API; sustituye a Grok Voice 2.0 al mismo precio (0,08 $/min), y xAI afirma que ocupa el primer puesto del índice Speech-to-Speech de Artificial Analysis. [TechEnclave](https://techenclave.com/news/items/xai-releases-grok-voice-3-and-upgrades-the-latest-api-alias)

**A tener en cuenta:**
- Gemini 4 Argon se anunció el 30 de septiembre solo para socios de ciberseguridad. Lo del 13 de octubre es la ampliación del acceso, no su primer anuncio.
- Todas las fuentes son medios o agregadores, no los blogs oficiales de cada empresa. Las cifras de rendimiento las dan los propios fabricantes y nadie las ha verificado de forma independiente.
- Dejé fuera "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017", que un agregador fecha el 17 de octubre. El modelo V4.1 Flash salió en septiembre y no pude confirmar esa versión en ninguna otra fuente.
- GPT-6 (OpenAI) y Claude Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic) salieron el 7 de octubre, justo antes de este periodo de 7 días.
